Ground-floor "cellules exiguës" (cramped cells) where captives were held by sex and age, a long dark corridor to the "Porte du voyage sans retour" opening onto the ocean, and a double-flight staircase to exhibition rooms.

Hypersaline lake coloured by the alga *Dunaliella salina*; the pink is strongest from late January to early March and visible November to May; you float. It lost its colour after 2022 when the State discharged Dakar floodwater into it (depth rose from 2.5 m to 6 m) and again after summer 2024 rains, regained it in 2025, and **salt extraction officially reopened on Jul 22, 2026** after four years, with about 3,000 harvesters back, salinity at 380 g/L and a 600 m drainage channel, though the colour is "less intense than before 2022" (that article has internal inconsistencies). Activities: pirogue rides of about 20 minutes, camel rides (30 minutes to the beach or 15 to the filao trees), quads, Land Rover and 4x4 tours to the dunes and ocean. The site is free to visit; guides sometimes block access to the artisan village.
